label: folio-assistant vocabulary (core only)
comment: Every class and property the folio knowledge graph projects, one node each. Generated by scripts/ns-export.ts; graph-typology definitions are read from the declaration registry rather than restated here.

@graph.label: computation-witness
@graph.comment: What a folio's computations recorded: one `<name>.witness.json` per producer run, naming the engine, the script and its hash, the commit, and each assertion with its computed and expected values. Written by the producer and regenerated by re-running it; addressable from prose and wired to a content block through `computation.witness`.

@graph.label: glossary
@graph.comment: SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1): local terms with definitions and codes, linked to external SKOS schemes by exactMatch rather than copied. Rendered on the glossary/ page.

@graph.label: public-comments
@graph.comment: A public-comment record — one `public-comment/1.0.0` JSON per comment under `comments/`, and one `changeset/1.0.0` JSON per change-set under `changesets/`. Written by the public-comment tool as comments are triaged and change-sets agreed.

@graph.label: review-verdicts
@graph.comment: Reviewers' per-block verdicts — one `folio-review-verdict/v1` JSON each, pinned to the block's content hash and committed on the edit-set's feature branch. Read by the review coverage gate (`folio-review-coverage`), which counts a verdict only while its hash is current.

@graph.label: Algorithm
@graph.comment: An algorithm must cite at least one provable label in `uses[]` (AlgorithmSchema): algorithms are downstream of the mathematics that justifies them.
@graph.definition: An algorithm must cite at least one provable label in `uses[]` (AlgorithmSchema): algorithms are downstream of the mathematics that justifies them.

@graph.label: Figure
@graph.comment: Shares `fig` with `diagram` on purpose. The prefix names what a reader CITES ("see fig:3"), and a reader does not care whether the figure was drawn in tikzcd or lifted out of a PDF. Its DoCO co-type is a fact, not a stretch: DoCO's Figure is a figure in a document, which is exactly what an extracted figure block is.

@graph.label: Prose
@graph.comment: Shown with no heading: the empty `heading` is deliberate, and `render-markdown` suppresses the title-cased fallback for it. `prefixEnforced: false` because LABEL_PREFIXES never carried `prose`: its label prefix is recognised (KNOWN_LABEL_PREFIXES has had `prose:` since 2026-08-26) but not required, and the move onto nodes keeps that rather than tightening it unannounced.

@graph.label: Recommendation
@graph.comment: Bean 55ao. The statement an L1 guidance document exists to make: cited, traced to and signed off one at a time, so labelled like a theorem, but proved by nothing; its authority is the issuing body's. `prefixEnforced: false` on the owner's ruling (2026-09-23, Q1): the FOLIO chooses its label grammar, so `rec` is recognised and never required. Strength is a code in a declared code list (Q2, see code-lists/); a link to a DAK health-intervention is the optional `about` edge, never a merge (Q3, 2026-10-06). No DoCO co-type: none is unambiguously right for a normative statement. Typed by cat-harness as `RecommendationBlock`.

@graph.label: Simulator
@graph.comment: No DoCO co-type: a simulator has no DoCO counterpart, and guessing one would put a wrong triple in a published graph.
